claims: A mortgage loan officer (MLO) or mortgage loan originator is a licensed professional.
Mortgage loan officers must register with the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System & Registry (NMLS).
A high school diploma or GED is required for mortgage loan officers.
Completion of at least 20 hours of NMLS-approved training is required for mortgage loan officers.
Mortgage loan officers must pass a national exam.
Mortgage loan officers must pass background checks.
Mortgage loan officers must get employer sponsorship.
Average base salaries for mortgage loan officers range from roughly $70,000 to over $85,000 annually.
Base salaries for mortgage loan officers are often supplemented by bonuses, commissions, and profit-sharing.
Bonuses, commissions, and profit-sharing for mortgage loan officers can exceed $40,000 yearly.
Mortgage loan officers require understanding of credit reports, debt-to-income ratios, and interest rates.
The role of mortgage loan officer requires 8 hours of annual training.
